items.context: The discovery flow needs a UI surface. The question is whether to add a new dedicated page or embed the flow within the existing BrandListPage. ScannerPage already demonstrates the pattern of a text input for scenario name on its own page.

options.label: New dedicated DiscoveryPage
options.rationale: Keeps BrandListPage simple. Follows the existing pattern where each flow has its own page (ScannerPage, StandardsPage). The discovery results view is complex enough (sources table, draft preview, suggestions, action buttons) to warrant its own page. Recommended because it avoids overloading BrandListPage.

options.label: Modal/dialog overlay on BrandListPage
options.rationale: Fewer navigation steps. User stays in context of their brand library. But the discovery results are too rich for a modal — source breakdown, color swatches, suggestions, and 3 action buttons would feel cramped.

items.context: When the user clicks 'Edit Before Importing', the discovered draft brand data needs to reach BrandFormPage. Since the app uses hash-based routing (no React Router with state), we need a mechanism to pass the draft brand object to the form page.

options.label: Session storage
options.rationale: Store the draft brand JSON in sessionStorage before navigating. BrandFormPage reads and clears it on mount. Simple, works with hash routing, survives the navigation, and is automatically cleaned up when the tab closes. Recommended for simplicity and compatibility with the existing routing.

options.label: URL-encoded query parameters
options.rationale: Encode the draft brand as base64 in the hash (e.g., /brands/new?prefill=...). Shareable/bookmarkable, but the draft brand can be large (especially with asset paths and all fields), making URLs unwieldy.

options.label: Zustand/global store
options.rationale: Add a lightweight store to hold discovery state. Clean React pattern, but introduces a new dependency (or requires custom context) for a single use case. Over-engineered for this need.

items.context: The discovery UI involves API calls, conditional rendering (loading/error/results states), and navigation flows. We need to decide what level of testing to apply. The existing codebase has Go tests for the API but no visible React test files in the UI src.

options.label: Go API integration tests only
options.rationale: The discovery endpoints are already tested in Go. Add tests for the new API client functions by testing the Go handlers with the expected request/response shapes. Skip React component tests since the existing UI has none. Recommended because it matches the current testing pattern and the UI is thin.

options.label: Go API tests + React component tests (vitest + testing-library)
options.rationale: More thorough coverage. Tests the discovery page rendering states and user interactions. But adds a new testing dependency and pattern that doesn't exist in this UI codebase yet — may be better suited as a separate initiative.

options.label: Scenario-level E2E tests via make test
options.rationale: Test the full flow end-to-end using the scenario test infrastructure. Most realistic validation but slower and more complex to set up.

items.context: The discovery result includes a confidence score (0.0-1.0) and per-source confidence. The UI needs to communicate this to the user in a way that's immediately understandable.

options.label: Traffic-light badge (High/Medium/Low)
options.rationale: Simple thresholds: ≥0.7 = green 'High', ≥0.4 = yellow 'Medium', <0.4 = red 'Low'. Immediately scannable. Consistent with existing ContrastBadge component pattern (pass/fail visual). Recommended for simplicity and consistency with existing UI patterns.

options.label: Progress bar with percentage
options.rationale: Shows the exact score visually. More precise but may imply false precision — a 0.65 vs 0.68 difference is not meaningful.

options.label: Star rating (1-5)
options.rationale: Familiar pattern but doesn't map cleanly to the 0-1 scale and may imply quality judgment rather than data coverage.

items.text: The brand-manager-scenario-picker backlog item is still in backlog status. That item would add a reusable scenario selector component. For this discovery UI, we'll use a simple text input for scenario name (matching the pattern in ScannerPage), which can be upgraded to the picker component once it's built.
